compatibility_badge: PCB Layout Change Required (Pinout or Package Mismatch)

pin_diff.note: CRITICAL OUTPUT STAGE DIFFERENCE: LM393DR is comparator (open-collector) vs LMV358IDR opamp (push-pull); a comparator is an uncompensated open-loop switching device (no internal Miller/dominant-pole compensation) and will oscillate or latch in a linear negative-feedback op-amp circuit, while an op-amp used as a comparator suffers slow saturation/overdrive recovery and propagation delay far worse than its slew rate implies; the open-collector/open-drain output can only sink current and requires an external pull-up resistor to reach logic-high, whereas the push-pull output actively drives both rails (a pull-up tied to a different rail can back-drive a push-pull stage).

Single SOT-23-5 op-amps vary in pin ordering across vendors; verify Pin 1–5.

swap_risks: CRITICAL OP-AMP VS COMPARATOR TRAP: LM393DR is a comparator with open-collector output while LMV358IDR is a opamp with push-pull output. Even with identical pinouts, a comparator is an uncompensated switching device: dropping it into a linear negative-feedback op-amp circuit (buffer, gain stage, filter) causes oscillation or latch-up, and an op-amp used as a comparator suffers slow overdrive/saturation recovery. In addition, the open-collector/open-drain output requires an external pull-up resistor to swing high.

CRITICAL SUPPLY VOLTAGE RATING: LMV358IDR is limited to 5.5 V max (5.5 V abs max, p.5) whereas LM393DR supports up to 30 V (36 V abs max, p.4). Installing a 5.5 V CMOS part on a 12 V–24 V rail causes instant breakdown.

HIGH HEADROOM / CLIPPING RISK: Rail-to-rail capability differs (LM393DR: IN=Non-RR, OUT=Non-RR vs LMV358IDR: IN=Non-RR, OUT=RR); verify input common-mode range (Vicm) and output voltage swing against ADC full-scale range.

CAUTION QUIESCENT CURRENT SHIFT: Supply current per channel differs by 2.1x (LM393DR: 225 µA/ch p.8 vs LMV358IDR: 105 µA/ch p.7); verify battery budget and total power dissipation across all channels.
HIGH ABSOLUTE-MAX SURGE MARGIN: LMV358IDR has a lower Vs,abs,max rating (5.5 V, p.5) than LM393DR (36 V, p.4); verify hot-plug, inductive kickback, and TVS clamp peaks stay safely below 5.5 V.
HIGH THERMAL MARGIN: Package θJA is 40% higher on LMV358IDR (LM393DR: 148.5 °C/W p.5 vs LMV358IDR: 207.9 °C/W p.6); re-check Tj = Ta + Pd × θJA against Tj,max.
HIGH MINIMUM SUPPLY FLOOR: LMV358IDR requires Vs,min >= 2.7 V (p.5) vs 2 V on the counterpart; confirm low-battery / brown-out operation still clears the higher floor.

HIGH TEMPERATURE GRADE MISMATCH: Rated ambient range differs (LM393DR: 0..70 °C Commercial (0°C to 70°C) vs LMV358IDR: -40..125 °C Extended Industrial (-40°C to 125°C)); LM393DR cold limit only 0 °C, LM393DR hot limit only 70 °C — verify product ambient qualification before swapping.
engineering_verdict: LM393DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and LMV358IDR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) are NOT drop-in interchangeable (Level 3 PCB Layout / Circuit Change Required) due to device kind mismatch (comparator/open-collector vs opamp/push-pull) — circuit redesign required. Specific pin conflicts: Pin 1 (OUT_A vs OUT_A), Pin 7 (OUT_B vs OUT_B). Signal-chain deltas: comparator (open-collector) vs opamp (push-pull), supply ceiling 30 V (p.4) vs 5.5 V (p.5), Vos 5 mV (p.8) vs 7 mV (p.7), Ib 2x gap (25000 vs 15000 pA). Primary bench gotchas to watch: LM393DR "Classic LM358DR / LMV358IDR Identical SOIC-8 Pinout Trap (Missing Pull-Up & Oscillation)" (p.3) and LMV358IDR "5.5 V Absolute Maximum Ceiling — Destructive If Swapped into LM358 High-Voltage Boards" (p.5). BOM decision: Choose LM393DR when the circuit is an open-loop threshold/window comparator (open-collector output) or supply rails exceed 5.5 V (rated up to 30 V); choose LMV358IDR when the circuit is a linear closed-loop amplifier, buffer, or active filter or ultra-low supply current (105 µA/ch) is prioritized. Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.3) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
